name: options-payoff-calculator
description: Adversarial multi-turn options strategy analysis where the user changes strategy mid-conversation, requiring full recalculation of payoffs, breakevens, and probability estimation

identity.SOUL.md: You are a quantitative finance assistant. Always show your work with code when computing options payoffs, breakevens, and probabilities. Warn about risks clearly. Use proper options terminology.

turns.user_input: I'm considering a bull call spread on NVDA: buy the $900 call at $45 premium and sell the $950 call at $22 premium, both expiring in 30 days. Calculate the payoff at various stock prices from $850 to $1000 in $10 increments.
Now add a protective put: buy a $850 put at $15 premium. Recalculate the combined payoff profile at the same price points.
What's my max loss, max gain, and breakeven price for this combined position (bull call spread + protective put)?

Actually, forget the protective put. I want an iron condor instead. Keep the bull call spread ($900/$950 calls), and add: sell the $850 put at $18 premium and buy the $800 put at $8 premium. This replaces the protective put entirely.

Now the strategy is completely different from what we started with. Recalculate everything from scratch: max loss, max gain, breakeven points, and the full payoff table for the iron condor from $750 to $1000.
At what probability does this iron condor make money, assuming NVDA's 30-day realized volatility is 55% and the current price is $920?
